## Decisions

- **Rename carry-over.** The mod was Ultima Kingdoms until 0.1.1. `persistence/LegacyRename` copies each
  `ultima_kingdoms_*.dat` and pre-rename config file once (only when the new name is absent, never deleting the
  old), rewriting `ultima_kingdoms:` ids and `.ultima_kingdoms.` keys; `CivicIdentityStore` moves the entity key
  on read; a `MissingMappingsEvent` remaps the two items. `LegacyRenameTest` fails if a new saved-data store or
  config file is added without a migration entry. A failed saved-data or common-config copy stops the world before any
  store exists (F03; `requireMigrated`), and `world/data/mcakingdoms_migration_report.txt` records each step.
- **Companions accept both ids** (Quests `KingdomIntegration`, Conversations `KingdomsIdentity`, Reputation's namespace
  gate, every `mods.toml`). Runtime aliases go only in a coordinated release after the companions are published and
  upgrade-tested; on-disk migration support stays (`docs/Upgrade-and-Recovery.md`).
- **Completion-receipt consumer.** Kingdoms polls as whatever `McaQuestsApi.institutionalCompletionConsumer()`
  names (fallback `mcakingdoms:regional_civic_network`), never its own spelling. Paid institutional work needs that
  method to name an `mcakingdoms` consumer: `QuestCompletionBridge.institutionalContract` probes methods only and
  `CivicService.workshop` refuses before any offer otherwise (F04). The companion tuple is `tools/test/companions.json`.
- **Townstead is probed, not version-matched.** Each capability binds member by member and fails closed;
  `politics_townstead_version` (the validated Townstead versions) and `townstead_validated_tuples` (Townstead@MCA pairs)
  are only reported. One backend per session (`v1`, `legacy`, `mca`, `none`), chosen in `TownsteadBackends`; buildings
  come from one source per session, MCA's loaded-village buildings when Townstead's query is absent
  (`TownsteadBinding.buildingFallback`). Only `compat/townstead/v1` may name a Townstead type, so nothing links to
  Townstead when it is absent (`TownsteadApiContractTest`); the v1 backend is loaded by reflection. The compile-only
  `libs/townstead-api` jar is built from the tagged 0.8.0 source (`-PtownsteadApiSources`, `buildTownsteadApi`) and
  checked by `verifyTownsteadApi` and against the published jar member by member.
- **Townstead is never written.** Kingdoms reads, asks for reactions and Chronicle stories, and keeps its own
  decisions and restored-backup baselines in `mcakingdoms_townstead.dat`. Political conflicts are reported, never merged;
  operator adopt/release/clear/acknowledge decide on the Kingdoms side only (`TownsteadAuthority.decideLocal`, pure and
  unit-tested). Chronicle projections are claimed before the call and never retried. No reward, payment or reservation
  comes from a Townstead event, story or stock count.
- **One contact distance.** `regional_civic_network.contactRange` bounds the `nearby_npc` picker and every guild
  and contract validator; MCA: Crime keeps its own 8-block workshop rule.
- **Mixins.** Forge 47 reads mixin configs only from the jar manifest (`MixinConfigs`); dev runs pass
  `-mixin.config=mcakingdoms.mixins.json`. `modmap.py`'s "Mixins: no" is a heuristic miss, not a fact: the config lists
  21 common mixins, each targeting a companion's class by name with `remap = false`: eight for Recruits, twelve for
  Living Villages and, since 0.3.1, the `@Pseudo` `WaystonesEditMixin`. `mixin/RecruitsMixinPlugin` filters them:
  Recruits mixins only with Recruits 1.15.2, `Lv*` through `LvGate`, `Waystones*` through `WaystonesGate`. There is no
  refmap and no mixin targeting a Minecraft class.
- **Petition honors** come from kingdom metadata `petition_honor` (default `mcakingdoms:open_bell`).
- **Village identity is the structure start; reconciliation merges fragments** into the record holding it (D1–D6 in
  `docs/MCAKingdoms-Village-Identity-Diagnosis-and-Plan.md`); compare stored settlement ids through `resolveSettlementId`.
- **Reload outcomes belong to one attempt** (`data/ReloadReport`). Six domains validate while the reload prepares, so a
  rejection there fails the whole reload; civic rules, world-context selectors, dynasty definitions (succession laws and
  court ranks) and development templates reject domain-locally at apply and keep their previous snapshot. `/kingdoms reload`, Reload server definitions and Server health all read the same attempt.
- **Kingdom Tasks protocol 4** (`interaction/InteractionNetwork`): the authorized task index (`INDEX`, now with group and
  availability; each distinct unavailability reason is sent once in `reasons`, without the English fallbacks the client
  translates itself, and entries name it by position `q`) is searched on the client in the player's language; record choices (`FILTER`) on the server in the three
  bundled languages. `START` returns the start view (`interaction/Suggestions`); replies carry the confirm label, a status
  (`done`, `waiting`, `refused`, `unknown`, or `read` for read-only tasks) and a Book topic. Handlers return a typed
  `ActionRegistry.Outcome` (applied, pending, refused, unknown, read); `CHECK` asks the task's registered `Probe` and never
  runs the handler again (F07). Other channels on 2026-10-27: main 7 (ledger search and sort, kingdom gallery, gallery
  stale notices, political notices, office badges), `civic` 4 (read-only structured guild view), `politics` 4 (record
  fields, header), `war_room` 4 (sections, per-link availability). Design note: `docs/Localized-Search-Design.md`.
- **Feature checks before forms.** `interaction/TaskMeta` maps each task to the server features it needs (config switches,
  companion mods, capability probes); an unavailable task is listed and explained, never opened as a form. The War Room
  marks its links the same way. Owning services still decide every request. `TaskMeta.Intent` keeps cleanup reachable:
  inspect and cancel need no feature; verify and restore need only their native provider (F08).
- **Requirement rows are projections.** `ActionRegistry.requirements`, `interaction/Requirements` and
  `civic/CivicRequirements` read each owning service's rule for display (`MET`, `UNMET`, `UNKNOWN`, or `NOTE` for
  information such as which route applies); they never decide anything.
- **Book resources are schema 2** (`guide/KingdomGuide`): typed blocks, legacy schema 1 adapted, lenient reading in game and
  strict reading in tests. Recipe blocks name a recipe id; `guide/GuideRecipe` builds the display from whichever
  `RecipeManager` it is given (the client's synchronized one in game, isolated managers in GameTests). Text may contain
  `{key:tasks}` only. Format: `docs/Datapack-Reference.md#book-of-kingdoms-pages`.
- **Manuscript interfaces (2026-10-26).** All Kingdoms-owned screens reuse `client/book` (materials, layout,
  buttons, search, native cycle/slider presentation, confirmation and illumination). `RichPanel.manuscript()` and `MenuTextPanel.manuscript()` opt into dark ink;
  operational pages use bounded folios. Wide books show facing leaves; Tasks uses a folio with two start
  columns. Narrow screens retain normal text size in one column. Guide page turns retain a line of overlap.
  `BookIllustrations` routes separate cached frontispieces to the Book, Ledger and Tasks. The material atlas contains crimson/green/
  walnut bindings and high-contrast leather control states. Ledger kingdom-picker pages and draggable local settlement
  rows are client-only; server result pagination and filter authority remain separate.
  `docs/Book-Interface-Design.md` records the interface inventory, asset provenance and acceptance evidence.
- **Rich panels** (`client/rich/RichPanel`, `Pieces`) render the Book, Guilds, Kingdom and War Room content with focusable
  link targets and a narration text for every piece. Client-only state (bookmarks, recents, favourites, last topic) lives
  in `config/mcakingdoms-client-state.json` (`client/ClientState`), never on the server.
- **Dedicated-server safety of client hooks.** Lambdas that mention client classes live in `client/ClientExtensions`, not
  in classes the dist check loads on a dedicated server (a GameTest server crashed on `Screen` once).
- **Resident founding** is decided by `GovernmentService.residentFounder`; Tasks and the command only constrain the
  choices. The `openFounding` setting is a `BooleanSupplier` in the package-private constructor so tests pass a fixed
  value: `ConfigValue.set` rewrites the file and Forge's watcher reloads it on another thread (the same race as the r3
  known issue below).
- **Translations are guarded by tests**, not by review: `TranslationCoverageTest` (task catalogue, enum labels, fact types,
  unavailability causes in en/es/zh), `LangCoverageTest`, `KingdomsHelpCommandsTest`, and `GuideTranslationTest`. A Book
  translation replaces the English entry whole by id, so it must keep the same links and commands.
- **Examples are executable.** `examples/datapack` (and its `invalid/` variants with `expected.txt`) is loaded by the
  `ExamplePack*Test` unit tests through the real loaders; `examples/addon` is compiled against the API jar by `check`.

- **Settlement loads are all-or-nothing** (F02). `SettlementSavedData.read` validates records, ids, bounds, redirects
  (cycles, dangling, live sources) and external references before anything is writable; a refusal keeps the original
  tag, is never dirty, and `get()` throws so the server stops. An existing but undecodable file is refused through
  `fresh(true)`. Tests are GameTests (`SettlementLoadRefusalGameTests`) because unit tests cannot bootstrap registries.
- **Maintenance is per domain** (F05): `GovernmentService.due` builds each domain's due list (deadline, then id, budget 8);
  evolution credits occupied time from presence, not consecutive samples (F06), and announces only after a commit (F09).
- **Capacity** (F12): `persistence/Capacity` inventories every bounded collection (`Capacity.all`, Server health,
  `/kingdoms maintenance capacity`). Only finished transfers and opportunities compact, dry run first, archive
  (`persistence/Archive`, `<world>/mcakingdoms_archive/`) before removal. Everything else refuses at its bound.
- **Settlement paging** (F13): `core/OrderedSettlements` keeps one sorted snapshot per store revision.
- **Residence registration** (A01): `citizen/ResidenceRegistration` owns the evidence policy (bed-set respawn point,
  loaded chunk, inside a recognized settlement, player present; provider player-home evidence first). Moves wait
  `residenceMoveCooldown` on overworld game time. Tasks live in `interaction/ResidenceTasks`; `/kingdoms residence`.
- **Political presentation** (A02): `politics/OfficePresentation` diffs offices on `PoliticalCommittedEvent`; notices are
  bounded (16 queued, 20 ticks apart) and audience-filtered; badges go `TRACKING_ENTITY_AND_SELF` only.
  `client/PoliticalPresentation` draws an additive line above the name tag and never touches names.
- **Living Villages is reflection-only** (`compat/livingvillages/LvAccess` resolves every member by exact name and
  signature; nothing is on the compile classpath). `mixin/LvGate` applies the `@Pseudo` `Lv*` mixins only to the audited
  1.1.0 jar (SHA-256) with Recruits 1.15.2, and `LvResidentGuardMixin` only in production, because its redirects name
  SRG methods. `LvCompat` is the one capability snapshot for tasks, the Book, status and every service. The bridge store
  (`mcakingdoms_living_villages`, JSON schema 1 in NBT, atomic) journals intent before a provider write and acknowledges
  it at the next Overworld save, once Living Villages' own data is no longer dirty. Realms are not kingdoms: a realm is a
  provider faction with a stable id, a kingdom represents one only through an operator association
  (`api/politics/PoliticalPartyRef`). Policies are pure functions in `LvPolicy` (unit-tested).
- **Settlement identity commits first** (AUD-01): a new settlement, a merge and a kingdom change are written by
  `SettlementSavedData.commitRoot` before any event; a failed write restores the snapshot and throws. The durable
  `IdentityOutbox` (optional key in the same file) carries each change to the other stores through
  `core/IdentityConsumers` (idempotent, `guarded` by store writability), run at start and every 1,200 ticks.
- **Inventory effects are confirmed, not forced** (AUD-02, AUD-09): `persistence/PlayerEvidence` puts a marker in
  `PlayerPersisted` in the same tick as the inventory change; `PlayerEvent.SaveToFile` (or, for a single-player owner,
  the end of the tick that wrote `level.dat`) confirms it, and login settles it from the copy loaded. No save is forced:
  a forced player save would run ahead of the chunks. Deliveries count provisionally; nothing irreversible depends on an
  unconfirmed one.
- **Construction is verified by saves** (AUD-03): `LevelEvent.Save` fires after chunks are handed to the async IO worker,
  so a placed cell moves APPLIED → SAVED → VERIFIED over two saves; a later run that loads it verifies it too.
- **Development keeps assets apart from history** (AUD-07): `DevelopmentSavedData` schema 2 holds productive assets,
  inventory operations and receipts with server-issued, time-stamped request ids (`persistence/RequestIds`) and a
  watermark; `retain` drops history only when its effects are kept elsewhere.
- **Waystones is reflection-only** (WAY-01): `compat/waystones/WaystonesAccess` binds Waystones 14.1.21 / Balm 7.3.44 by
  exact version and member; naming listens to the two Balm events, and `WaystonesEditMixin` observes accepted edits only
  on the tested jar (`WaystonesGate`, SHA-256). One-time naming; `WaystonesNamingData` records each name before it is
  handed over and confirms it at the next save.
- **Portable acceptance** (F16): `tools/test/environment.py` resolves the EULA, installation, pack, Java, Xvfb and
  wrapper from `MCAKINGDOMS_*` variables or the ignored `tools/test/local-environment.json`. Historical provider-patch
  checks live in `tools/history/`.

## Known issues

- **Packaged `r3` acceptance (fixture fixed in 0.3.0, F16).** The 2026-10-01 intermittent failure at "saved native siege
  appears in history" was attributed to `WarfareScenario` toggling `WarfareConfig.MILITARY` mid-run while Forge's config
  watcher reloaded the file on another thread. `integration_runtime.py` now writes `militaryActions = false` into the
  isolated fixture config before launch, the scenario no longer toggles it, and it asserts the native `isUnderSiege` flag
  immediately after `setUnderSiege`. On 2026-10-27 the packaged R3 sequence passed all five boots (r3, restart, Recruits absent, reinstalled,
  future schema) in three runs on jar `812e3e41`, three on the pre-fix `d0f578bd` and one on the release jar `0dd679e4`; the
  saved native siege reached history every time (`build/v030-evidence/runtime/`). The audit handoff (H01) also routed
  warfare reads through `WarfareConfig.enabled()`, and on 2026-10-28 `r3` passed 20 consecutive packaged runs on one
  build, five boots each (`build/v030-evidence/audit/runtime/final-r3-*`). The earlier failure was intermittent, so these
  passes support the race explanation rather than prove it; keep the immediate siege-flag assertion.
- **Companion contract unpublished.** The public MCA Quests 1.7.1 source lacks `institutionalCompletionConsumer()`; the
  validated pack jar was built from local work. Kingdoms reports `legacy_consumer_contract` and refuses paid workshop jobs.
- Advancement and statistics progress recorded under `ultima_kingdoms:` is migrated only when an operator turns on
  `migration.legacyProgress` (H09, `persistence/LegacyProgress`); recipe-book entries are never rewritten and unlock
  again when the items are held.
- The R1–R3 provider patches under `docs/history/provider-patches/` still name `ultima_kingdoms`; they are a record and
  must not be applied. Their old verification lives in `tools/history/verify_r2_provider_exports.py`.
- **Living Villages limits.** Its live wars and abstract sieges exist only in memory, so after a restart the bridge
  continues a recorded war as an abstract siege. Its map markers go to every player. Road grading between its own
  buildings and the fixed layout of command-founded villages are not checked by `protectExternalBuildings`. Development
  runs cannot apply the resident guard (SRG names); use the packaged `lv` phases.
- **Townstead limits.** Townstead 0.8.0 accepts no external government, so a released or adopted settlement still has
  Townstead's own council running inside Townstead; Chronicle stories need a player present; civic and village names
  are not synchronized. Townstead 0.8.0 requires exactly MCA 7.7.1-beta.5, so it cannot be tested beside the pack's
  MCA 7.6.26. Packaged fixtures that recognize an MCA building must give it its required blocks (MCA's completion is a
  block count, `TownsteadScenario.blocks`), and its type must be defined by data: MCA gives an undefined type a
  billion-bed requirement. No MCA or Townstead release defines `workshop`, the Lamplighters' family, so the acceptance
  mod defines it (`tools/test/runtime/resources/data/mcakingdoms_acceptance/building_types/workshop.json`); a pack must too.
- Generated-section heuristics: the language row counts only `en_us`, `es_es`, `zh_cn` files (each holds every key), and
  "Mixins: no" is a miss (see Decisions).
- **0.3.0 audit decisions.** Every A–D feature defaults to doing nothing on upgraded worlds (law Manual only,
  `development.mode = OFF`); Capitals is read-only; the development store is written only above `OFF`, and under Manual
  only the dynasty store records just each throne's ruler and, for a vacancy, a case left to officials (with a memorial
  after a death); test seams
  `DevelopmentMode.overrideForTests`, `WarfareConfig.overrideEnabledForTests` and `DynastyService`'s explicit constructor
  replace config rewrites in tests. GameTest worlds generate no natural villages
  (`src/gameTest/resources/data/minecraft/worldgen/structure_set/villages.json`, frequency 0): the village identity
  tests use random coordinates, and a real village beside one once took its record.
